note: Aman drawn from the corpus by the Arda Archive. No map of this land exists in Christopher Tolkien's hand; the outline, the coastline and every coordinate here are the archive's own work and carry no authority but their own. What the corpus establishes is the RELATION recorded on each feature, never the position.

placed.q: west shores looked upon the Outer Sea, that is called by the Elves Ekkaia
placed.attests: the Outer Sea lies off the WEST shore of Aman

placed.q: the east shores of Aman were the uttermost end of Belegaer, the Great Sea of the West
placed.attests: the Great Sea lies off the EAST shore of Aman

placed.q: upon the shores of the sea they raised the Pelóri, the Mountains of Aman, highest upon Earth
placed.attests: the mountains stand ON the eastern shore, between the sea and what lies behind them

placed.q: above all the mountains of the Pelóri was that height upon whose summit Manwë set his throne
placed.attests: the highest peak OF the Pelóri, therefore on the range
placed.infer: the corpus fixes Taniquetil THREE times: the highest of the Pelóri; 'standing upon the margin of the sea' (Silm:2732); and — the one that places it ALONG the range — 'Túna beneath Taniquetil' (Silm, Flight of the Noldor) [C], where Túna is 'The green hill in the Calacirya' by Silm's own index [C]. Drawn beside the pass on those two, not on the Vanyar inference given here until 12 Aug

placed.q: Behind the walls of the Pelóri the Valar established their domain in that region which is called Valinor
placed.attests: Valinor lies BEHIND the mountains — that is, west of them

placed.q: in the midst of the plain beyond the mountains they built their city, Valmar of many bells
placed.attests: in the MIDDLE of the plain, beyond the mountains from the sea

placed.q: Before its western gate there was a green mound, Ezellohar, that is named also Corollairë
placed.attests: immediately WEST of Valmar, before its western gate — where the Two Trees stood

placed.q: the Máhanaxar, the Ring of Doom near to the golden gates of Valmar
placed.attests: NEAR the gates of Valmar
placed.infer: 'near to the golden gates' fixes it beside the city but not on which side; it is drawn by Ezellohar because the Valar sat in it to hear Yavanna sing upon the mound

placed.q: a gap was made in the great walls of the Pelóri
placed.attests: a GAP THROUGH the range — the only breach in the mountain wall

placed.q: there in a deep valley that ran down to the sea the Eldar raised a high green hill: Túna it was called
placed.attests: IN the valley of the gap, on the seaward side

placed.q: Upon the crown of Túna the city of the Elves was built, the white walls and terraces of Tirion
placed.attests: ON the crown of Túna

placed.q: the highest of the towers of that city was the Tower of Ingwë, Mindon Eldaliéva
placed.attests: the highest tower OF Tirion

placed.q: to the east it looked towards the Bay of Elvenhome, and the Lonely Isle, and the Shadowy Seas
placed.attests: EAST of Túna, seen from the hill

placed.q: stood there alone in the Bay of Eldamar; and it was called Tol Eressëa, the Lonely Isle
placed.attests: IN the Bay of Eldamar

placed.q: it lay upon the confines of Eldamar, north of the Calacirya
placed.attests: NORTH of the Calacirya, on the coast of Eldamar

placed.q: This land lay northward between the Mountains of the Pelóri and the Great Sea
placed.attests: NORTH, and BETWEEN the mountains and the sea — a coastal strip east of the range

placed.q: came through the great mists of Oiomúrë to the Helcaraxë
placed.attests: between Araman and the Helcaraxë — passed through on the way north

placed.q: the strait between Araman and Middle-earth was filled with grinding ice
placed.attests: the strait at the NORTH, between Araman and Middle-earth

placed.q: That narrow land lay south of the Bay of Eldamar, beneath the eastern feet of the Pelóri
placed.attests: SOUTH of the bay, at the EASTERN foot of the mountains, and narrow

placed.q: northward in Valinor they made a strong place and treasury in the hills
placed.attests: NORTHWARD within Valinor, in hills

placed.q: Námo the elder dwells in Mandos, which is northward in Valinor
placed.attests: NORTHWARD within Valinor, near where Feanor dwelt and built Formenos
placed.infer: the published Silmarillion reads 'westward' and Christopher Tolkien calls that his own change and 'a regrettable error'; the final text of the Valaquenta has 'northward'. Placed north-of-centre beside Formenos because Feanor 'dwelt northward in Valinor near to the halls of Mandos'. The compass direction is Tolkien's final text; the exact spot is the archive's.

placed.q: Her halls are west of West, upon the borders of the world
placed.attests: the FURTHEST west — at the world's border, beyond Valinor proper

placed.q: And in the midst of the Blessed Realm were the mansions of Aulë, and there he laboured long
placed.attests: in the MIDST of the Blessed Realm

placed.q: Their halls are above the everlasting snow, upon Oiolossë, the uttermost tower of Taniquetil
placed.attests: ON the summit of Taniquetil, above the snowline

placed.q: he dwelt from the beginning of Arda in the Outer Ocean, and still he dwells there
placed.attests: Ulmo dwells in Ekkaia — OUTSIDE Valinor, and outside Aman altogether

placed.q: she walks not by day, but sleeps upon an island in the tree-shadowed lake of Lórellin
placed.attests: a lake with an island, in Lórien
placed.infer: the corpus places Lórellin IN Lórien, and Lórien only 'in the land of the Valar'. Where in that land is nowhere stated. It is drawn on the plain south of Valmar as a position that contradicts nothing, and for no better reason than that

unplaced.q: In Lórien are his gardens in the land of the Valar, and they are the fairest of all places in the world
unplaced.why: 'in the land of the Valar' is the whole of it. Lórien is placed nowhere within Valinor, and the lake of Lórellin is placed only within Lórien

unplaced.q: Oromë loved the lands of Middle-earth, and he left them unwillingly
unplaced.why: Oromë's woods in Aman are named but never sited; what the corpus places is his riding in Middle-earth, which is a different thing
